summary: Next.js App Router pages and API routes for the blog-starter scaffold template, demonstrating how to build a real content-driven site on top of the Barkpark JS SDK with draft-mode preview, webhook revalidation, and content relationships (posts, authors, tags).

intentions.title: Lower the time-to-first-working-site for new adopters
intentions.evidence: All 7 files together form a runnable blog; page.tsx + tags/page.tsx + authors/page.tsx give a complete content graph out of the box so a scaffolded project starts with real pages, not stubs

intentions.title: Demonstrate draft-mode (preview) as a first-class SDK pattern
intentions.evidence: draft-preview.tsx uses useOptimisticDocument from @barkpark/nextjs/actions; page.tsx branches on draftMode() to swap in the preview component; api/preview/route.ts and api/exit-preview/route.ts handle enter/exit lifecycle

intentions.title: Show webhook-driven ISR cache invalidation as the canonical publish flow
intentions.evidence: api/barkpark/webhook/route.ts wires createWebhookHandler + revalidateBarkpark, with inline comment instructing users to set BARKPARK_WEBHOOK_SECRET and point Studio at the route

intentions.title: Prove the SDK's optimistic-edit API with a concrete UI example
intentions.evidence: draft-preview.tsx exposes a commitOptimistic stub and an 'Optimistic edit title' button, explicitly inviting users to wire it to a real server action

intentions.title: Teach relationship traversal (refs) using the SDK client helpers
intentions.evidence: page.tsx resolves author and tags via getDocById using _ref fields; tags/page.tsx filters posts client-side by tag._id, showing both patterns (server join via ref and in-memory filter)
